sample.universe: A randomly selected 10 per cent population sample of individuals born between 1982 and 1989 (inclusive) in Denmark: 62,639 individuals

selection_rules: start from a randomly selected 10 per cent population sample of individuals born between 1982 and 1989 (inclusive): 62,639 individuals
select those with a NEET occurrence (measured during November each year) between ages 16 and 24: 26,483 individuals
deselect individuals who died during the observation period (44)
deselect individuals staying abroad for more than 12 months (10,121)
deselect a few with missing information on ethnicity (4)
resulting study population: 16,314 young adults (26 per cent of the full sample, Table A1)
sample.period: ages 16 to 24 for birth cohorts 1982-1989; a 108-month (nine-year) observation window per individual. Calendar years are not stated.

construction_notes: NEET follows the Eurostat / Statistics Denmark definition (equation 1, p. 6): number of young people not in employment, education or training divided by the total population of young people.
A NEET occurrence is measured during November of each year between ages 16 and 24.
Each individual is assigned a sequence of 108 months (equal to nine years).
State alphabet: NEET01, NEET02, NEET03, NEET04, NEETPLUS (five or more NEET occurrences between ages 16 and 24) and OTHER (all activities besides NEET, including employment or education).

Pairwise dissimilarity between sequences is computed with the Dynamic Hamming measure, which relies exclusively on data-based and time-dependent transformations (Lesnard, 2006, 2010) rather than insertions and deletions.

The alignment output is clustered; a six-cluster solution (A-F) is chosen, informed by cluster quality measures (Studer, 2013) and by the temporal and sociodemographic distinction between clusters C and D.
Plots made using the TraMineR package in R.

The Danish NEET indicator, unlike the Eurostat indicator, does not include non-formal educational activities; neither indicator counts activities outside the labour force (counselling, upskilling, job training, subsidized work) as education or employment, so participants in such interventions are classified as NEET.
Sociodemographic variables: gender, ethnicity, education level (at age 24) and family status (at age 16).
The activation variables record only whether an individual has ever experienced unemployment-related activation, or activation in relation to other NEET statuses, during the observation period.
Counts in Tables 1, 2 and A1 are printed with a Danish thousands separator ('11.593' = 11,593; '16.314' = 16,314; '62.639' = 62,639).

prior_findings_compared.as_stated: Accordingly, the article confirms Quintini and Martin's (2006) finding that, for most young adults, the NEET status is only transitory.

This analytical distinction, revealed by the longitudinal framework, confirms the necessity, also demonstrated in recent comparative studies (e.g., Holte et al., 2019), to discuss the relevance and applicability of the NEET concept across different welfare settings.
